pull_request.title: feat(vitruvian-sdk): a tool can act on a timer
pull_request.body:
Stage E of issue #3130, Task 1 (plan: PR #3183), alone in its PR because it cuts an SDK release: the Swift kit gains `Tool.every(seconds:_:)`, a handler the kit's one thread runs between messages, never while a handler runs or waits for the app, not before the hello; a handler that runs late runs once; an error it throws goes to the tool's log. The GitHub tool polls with it. The guide says how.

This release is the SDK's **1.0.0**: the commit carries `Release-As: 1.0.0` (release-please keeps the minor below 1.0 otherwise; the design's row D names 1.0.0 for protocol 2, which is on main).

**Checked:** kit tests 20 → 23; `guide_test`, the site sync's `in_sync_test` (the guide's copy is in this PR); the protocol pin did not move (kit only); licence check and verify; `//:tidy`. The planted regression (the timer's first deadline not set at the hello) failed four checks and was reversed. The three new tests are timing-based (50 ms ticks, a 3 to 8 window over 300 ms); they passed four runs here, and the plan accepted the window.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits:
feat(vitruvian-sdk): a tool can act on a timer

The Swift kit gains Tool.every(seconds:_:): a handler the kit's one
thread runs between messages, on Wire.next's deadline. It never runs
while a command's or a panel's handler runs or waits for the app, and
not before the app has said hello; a handler that runs late runs once;
an error it throws goes to the tool's log and the timer goes on. The
guide says so, and the site's copy of the guide is synced.

Stage E of tools for everyone, Task 1 (#3130). The protocol does not
change, so the app's pin does not move.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
